title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2019
short_title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit exports of live animals for slaughter from 1 July 2022 and impose animal welfare conditions on exports during the transition.
Export licences would cease authorising those shipments, while interim approvals would require satisfactory treatment overseas or a transitional exemption relating to certain existing contracts.
The legislation would begin on royal assent, with the interim framework operating before the permanent prohibition and allowing the secretary to consider overseas obligations and export history.
changes: Exporters would have to take reasonable steps to ensure satisfactory treatment of animals in the destination country.
Licence holders would have to notify the secretary within 14 days if satisfactory treatment had not occurred.
Satisfactory treatment would require specified holding, transport and slaughter standards, including stunning before slaughter.
summary.affected: Live-stock exporters and the Secretary are affected.
